about.title: King City Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: King City's economy leans heavily on agriculture, food processing, and transportation, and workers in these fields face real risks: machinery accidents, falls, vehicle collisions on routes like S 1st Street, and repetitive strain from long shifts. When someone is injured on the job here, California law usually channels the claim through workers' compensation, regardless of who was at fault. But that's not always the end of the story. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to the injury, a separate third-party claim may be possible alongside workers' comp. Navigating both systems can be confusing, especially while recovering. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect injured workers in King City with an independent attorney who can review the details, explain the options, and help figure out whether a third-party claim applies. There's no cost to get connected, and no obligation to move forward.

items.title: Understanding Your 30-Day Reporting Window
items.desc: California requires injured workers to report the incident to their employer within 30 days. An attorney can help make sure this step is handled correctly so it doesn't jeopardize a claim.

items.title: Spotting Third-Party Liability
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against an employer, but if a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment maker played a role, a separate claim may be available. That third-party claim carries its own 2-year deadline, so timing matters.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: Retaliation for reporting a workplace injury is illegal in California. An independent attorney can explain what protections apply if an employer responds poorly to a claim.

items.question: I work in agriculture near King City — does workers' comp still apply if I was hurt using a contractor's equipment?
items.answer: Generally yes, workers' compensation still applies to the employer relationship regardless of fault. But if the equipment was owned or maintained by a separate contractor or manufacturer, there may also be a third-party claim worth reviewing. An independent attorney can look at the specifics and explain which paths are available.

items.question: How long do I have to report my injury to my employer in King City?
items.answer: California law generally requires injured workers to notify their employer within 30 days of the injury. Missing this window can complicate a workers' comp claim, so it's worth reporting as soon as possible, even if the injury seems minor at first.

items.question: What if my injury happened in a vehicle accident while working, maybe near S 1st Street or Broadway Street?
items.answer: Work-related vehicle collisions often involve both a workers' comp claim and a potential third-party claim against another driver. Since third-party claims carry a 2-year deadline in California, it helps to get the facts reviewed early. LawProactive can connect you with an attorney who handles both sides of these claims.
